what: class-level external validation of the generality engine vs published network meta-analyses
method: engine ranking/lead read programmatically from each class league JSON; concordance judged at class-direction / top-tier / no-clean-winner level (not numeric effect match); every reference DOI resolved on PubMed.

entries.published_finding: Among PCSK9i monotherapy vs placebo, LDL-C reduction ranked evolocumab (MD -1.89) > alirocumab (-1.83) > inclisiran (-1.68 mmol/L).
entries.our_finding: engine ranks the overlapping agents evolocumab > alirocumab > inclisiran (lead overall bococizumab, a withdrawn agent NOT in the published network).

concordance.basis: inclisiran ranks last among the three shared agents in BOTH analyses; PCSK9i all lower LDL-C.
concordance.honest_note: our overall lead bococizumab was withdrawn and is absent from the published network; comparison is restricted to the evolocumab/alirocumab/inclisiran overlap. Jiang pools combination arms; we model %LDL monotherapy.

entries.published_finding: SGLT-2 inhibitors reduced heart-failure hospitalisation (and end-stage renal disease) as a class; no clean within-class efficacy winner is crowned.
entries.our_finding: engine: all SGLT2 agents reduce HF hospitalisation (lead canagliflozin HR 0.67), but every contrast is Low/Very-low certainty -> no clean within-class winner.

concordance.basis: class-level direction matches (SGLT2i reduce HF hosp); both decline to crown a within-class winner.
concordance.honest_note: Tsapas is a broad glucose-lowering NMA reporting SGLT2i at class level, not a canagliflozin-vs-empagliflozin-vs-dapagliflozin head-to-head; our nominal canagliflozin lead is explicitly Low-certainty, consistent with that.

entries.published_finding: For PASI-90, anti-IL17 and anti-IL23 biologics beat anti-TNF; the most effective (high-certainty) were infliximab, bimekizumab, ixekizumab, risankizumab.
entries.our_finding: engine lead bimekizumab (89.0% PASI-90); reproduces IL-17/IL-23 > TNF with P(IL-17/23>TNF)=1.0.

concordance.basis: our lead bimekizumab sits in Sbidian top tier (bimekizumab/ixekizumab/risankizumab); the anti-IL17/IL23 > TNF hierarchy is reproduced.
concordance.honest_note: Sbidian also ranks infliximab numerically highest, but its RR (50.19) is inflated by small/old trials and infliximab is outside our drug list; the modern top tier agrees.

entries.published_finding: All biologics had similar efficacy with no statistically significant rate-ratio differences; tezepelumab had numerically the lowest AAER and ranked first.
entries.our_finding: engine ranks tezepelumab first (IRR 0.48), all agents reduce the rate, but flags I2-type heterogeneity -> no clean 'best biologic'.

concordance.basis: both rank tezepelumab numerically first AND both decline statistical superiority of any single biologic — a precise two-part match including the self-flagging.
concordance.honest_note: identical headline behaviour: nominal tezepelumab lead + explicit "no clean winner".

entries.published_finding: Biologics+MTX improved ACR50 vs MTX (RR 1.40, absolute +16%, NNTB 7); evidence downgraded for INCONSISTENCY, with no clean within-class winner.
entries.our_finding: engine: all agents improve ACR response (lead etanercept); heterogeneity_flag=True (proportional-odds residual RMSE 2.035) -> ranking confounded, no clean winner.

concordance.basis: class-level ACR benefit matches; crucially our heterogeneity flag mirrors Cochrane's inconsistency downgrade — both say "no clean within-class winner".
concordance.honest_note: Singh 2017 is MTX-naive and pre-JAK (no tofacitinib/upa/bari data); our placebo-anchored ACR50 NNT (~1.4-5.9) is NOT the published biologic-vs-MTX incremental NNTB (7) — different contrast, stated openly.

entries.class: Oncologic imaging modalities (diagnostic test accuracy, bivariate Se/Sp)
entries.published_finding: Network meta-analysis of FDG-PET/(CT), CT and ultrasound for preoperative nodal staging: the modalities have COMPLEMENTARY diagnostic roles (highest-SUCRA test differs by nodal compartment), i.e. no single modality is uniformly best.
entries.our_finding: engine ranks CT nominally first by Youden J (0.732), but every cross-modality contrast is Low certainty and heterogeneity_flag=True (the AACT network mixes cancer sites) -> complementary roles, no clean winner.

concordance.basis: both decline to crown a single best modality: the engine's "no clean winner" (all cross-modality Youden-J differences imprecise + cross-target heterogeneity flag) matches Kim's "complementary diagnostic roles" conclusion.
concordance.honest_note: Kim 2021 is thyroid-specific (PET/CT/US, no MRI) using SUCRA on full-text 2x2 tables; ours is a pan-cancer registry-RECONSTRUCTED bivariate league (PET/MRI/CT/US, round(Se%xn1) cells, mixed target sites). The shared, validated claim is the "complementary / no-uniform-winner" hierarchy, NOT a modality-by-modality Se/Sp match.

honest_boundary: this is corroboration at the level the abstracts support, not a re-pooling of the published data; contrasts differ across analyses and each entry records its boundary. Registry-native (AACT) engine vs full-SR published NMAs.
